page: Amazon Web Services inf1.xlarge is an instance within the inf1 family, utilizing the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity stands at 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or discrete GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest CPU and memory performance. The Intel Xeon processor achieves average single-core performance in stress-ng and gzip compression tests, but multi-core execution is generally weak, as seen in the stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read and write speeds for large blocks categorized as weak. For specialized tasks, the instance achieves an average text generation speed of 75.74 tokens per second on a small 135M LLM model, though prompt processing speeds remain low.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inf1.xlarge offers an entry-level compute-oriented hardware profile with dedicated vCPUs. Given the weak multi-core and database benchmark results, this instance is appropriate for lightweight compute tasks, basic single-threaded applications, or entry-level machine learning inference workloads that fit within its 8.0 GB memory envelope and do not require local storage.
